This ticket is the code that turns the model's role-tagged blocks into the stored lesson, so the model never writes a node, a time or a safety tip placement (DIR-3).

tickets.title: ydoc: Lesson ↔ Y.Doc conversion, canonical hash, state vector, `covers`
tickets.story_text: US-25 — As an approver (P-3) I need to approve one pinned version, so that "approved" means a named person approved exactly that text. Platform work: the live document is a Y.Doc, the stored copy is JSON with a hash, and Submit must prove the stored state covers what the submitter holds. This package is the only place that crosses between them (HP-4, SP-2).

tickets.title: checks: kernel — registry with one shell per rule group, `CheckPolicy` (quote span ≥ 3, name scan blocking in `cfu_item` only, reviewer quote ≤ 12), Submit/Approve gates, structural rules (schema, sections, minutes, ELD callouts, CFU keys, heading order, table headers)
tickets.story_text: US-16 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need the issue list to refresh after each save, so that I know at once if an edit broke a rule, such as deleting the only question that checks a standard. This ticket is the kernel every rule plugs into: one registry with a stub for each of the 28 check kinds, the policy numbers SP-3 set, the pure Submit and Approve gates, and the structural rules, so the later rule tickets (NL-39, 40, 41) each fill their own files and edit nothing shared (Metz C1).

tickets.title: review: lesson state machine `decide_transition` (roles, states, UXP-1/3/4/10)
tickets.story_text: US-24 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need Submit to freeze the lesson, so that the approver reads exactly what I sent. US-25 — As an approver (P-3) I need to approve one pinned version. US-28 — reopening asks for a reason and makes a new version. This ticket is the one rule table for those moves, shared by the web app (most moves) and the collaboration server (Submit, the editable-state guard).

tickets.title: generation: pipeline state, `route_after_checks`, circuit breaker (pure)
tickets.story_text: US-8 — As an outline author (P-2) I need failed lessons to say why they failed and to be retried on their own, and a run to stop cleanly at its cap or after repeated failures, so that a few failures leave the rest of the unit reviewable and nothing is billed twice. This ticket is the pure decision layer: what the worker does next, which reason a failed tile shows, and when a run pauses, kept apart from every model call and database write (rule `agent-architecture`: code decides what next and don

tickets.title: platform: `Dockerfile.web`, `Dockerfile.node`, full Compose stack (Postgres unpublished, internal token), committed `render.yaml` (PD-15 D)
tickets.story_text: Platform work, no US of its own: the demo runs locally under Docker Compose with the deploy config committed (PD-15 option D: no new hosting spend). This ticket makes the three Node processes and Postgres start together, migrate once, record that they started, and keep the database and secrets off the host and out of the images.

tickets.title: web-ui: generated API client, Prism mock harness, mock collaboration server, app frame (nav, session redirect, can't-load and stale conventions), dialog and editor shells; SCR-1 sign in
tickets.story_text: US-37 — As a reviewer, author or approver (P-1, P-2, P-3), I need to sign in with an allow-listed staff email and see the actions my role can do. Platform work: every frontend ticket (NL-55…NL-76) builds on the client, mock harness, frame and shells made here, so none of them waits for a backend ticket.

tickets.title: auth: seeded-account sign-in, session resolve, sign-out, `middleware.ts`; fills auth wiring
tickets.story_text: US-37 — As a reviewer, author or approver (P-1, P-2, P-3), I need to sign in with an allow-listed staff email and password and be recognised by every later request, so that I see and do only what my role allows. Without this none of the other 23 routes can tell who is asking.

tickets.title: intake: upload and public-sheet import as numbered, hashed versions; Sheets fetcher; outline/standard repos; fills intake wiring
tickets.story_text: US-1 and US-2 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to upload the unit outline as CSV or XLSX, or paste a public Google Sheet link, and get a numbered, hashed version, so that every run can say exactly which outline it came from and re-uploading never touches a lesson.

tickets.title: runs: start a run (scope, pinned prompt, cap, idempotency, choices copy, jobs in one tx), run repo, run state machine
tickets.story_text: US-6 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to choose which rows to generate, see the prompt version the run will use, and set a spend cap, then start the run, so that a unit is generated once, under a ceiling, from a pinned prompt and a pinned set of intake choices.

tickets.title: generation: job queue — fair-share `SKIP LOCKED` claim, lease, requeue expired, cancel, retry failed, one candidate per lesson
tickets.story_text: US-8 — As an outline author (P-2), I need a run to survive a worker restart and failed lessons to be retried on their own, so that a killed worker costs at most the calls in flight and no lesson is stored or paid for twice. This ticket is the queue underneath that promise.

tickets.title: generation: lesson/candidate job runner and nodes (reserve, draft, compile-check, one repair on required-block misses, truncation retry, store, settle, fail; safety flags at v1)
tickets.story_text: US-7 — As an outline author (P-2), I need each lesson to be drafted, checked, repaired at most once and stored as a numbered draft with its full provenance, or to fail with a stated reason, so that the board shows ready lessons I can open and honest reasons for the rest.

tickets.title: generation: claim loop (cap 6, lease renewal, expired-lease requeue at start) and run finalizer (terminal, `partial`, `paused`, completeness query)
tickets.story_text: US-8 — As an outline author (P-2), I need the worker to keep at most six lessons in flight, to pick up exactly where a killed worker stopped, and to move a run to complete, partial, paused or capped by itself, so that a 47-lesson unit finishes without me watching it and a restart costs at most the calls in flight.

tickets.title: generation: UnitPlan job, stored before any lesson claim
tickets.story_text: US-9 — As an outline author (P-2), I need one plan for the whole unit — a line for every teaching day with what it hands forward — written and stored before any lesson is drafted, so that lessons are written against one consistent plan and I can read it first.

tickets.title: llm: Anthropic adapter (only SDK importer; schema-enforced mode for UnitPlan, plain + Zod for drafts), stub provider, price table
tickets.story_text: Platform work — it enables US-6, US-7 and US-8 (every generation call), CON-16 candidates and CON-17 AI suggestions. It is the one place a provider key is used and the one place the provider is replaced by a deterministic stand-in, so tests, capture checks, faults and load never spend money.

tickets.title: llm: model-call recorder (row before send, raw output on arrival, retries, 240 s timeout, lost calls) and `model_call` log
tickets.story_text: US-32 — As a content lead (P-3), I need one trace per run whose totals equal the sums over the stored calls, with cost taken from the provider's usage fields, so that I can trust what the batch cost. This ticket makes sure no call is ever invisible: the row exists before the send, the raw answer is saved the moment it arrives, and lost calls are counted.

tickets.title: prompts: prompt versions — list, current, v1 from the locked hash, no locked-layer write path; fills prompts wiring
tickets.story_text: US-10 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to see the locked prompt layer (read-only) and every guidance version, and to start each run on exactly one of them, so that I know which instructions produced a lesson and nobody can edit the rules that keep the output safe. Saving guidance is a later ticket (NL-88, cut #7); this one makes the versions exist, list and pin.

tickets.title: spend: reservation decision and atomic ledger (run cap, user-day cap, $75 build ceiling)
tickets.story_text: US-8 — As an outline author (P-2), I need a run to stop at its cap and never spend past it, even with six calls in flight, and the project to stop at the $75 build ceiling, so that no run, retry or AI suggestion can overspend. Money is decided in one pure function and written under one lock.

tickets.title: collab: lesson document store transaction (Y.Doc + derived JSON + hash + state vector + `check_job`), v1 seeding, web-side `HttpCollabCommandClient`
tickets.story_text: US-15 — As a reviewer (P-1), I need my edits stored durably together with the checks that follow them, and edits made from other screens (standards, slots, adopt, accept) to go through the same single writer, so that what I see, what is checked and what I later submit are one document. This ticket is the store transaction and the web side of the private call into the collaboration server.

tickets.title: checks: coalesced check queue and issue repository keyed to content hash
tickets.story_text: US-16 — As a reviewer (P-1), I need the issue list to refresh after each save and to tell me when a newer save is still being checked, so that I know at once whether an edit broke a rule and never trust a stale list. This ticket is the queue that makes checks run once per stored hash and the table that keeps issues tied to the hash they were computed on.

tickets.title: checks: check-context loader shared by worker, Submit freeze and Approve
tickets.story_text: US-12 — As a reviewer (P-1), I need to see that a lesson depends on another lesson and to be stopped from approving it before its source is ready, so the checks need the other lesson's stored text, the pending suggestions and the open safety flags. Three callers (the check worker, the Submit freeze and Approve) must build the same context, or the blocking set would differ between the issue list, Submit and Approve.

tickets.title: checks: alignment (taught + checked; listed / narrowed / added; leaf only), safety (tip present, no 6-word leak, disclosure prompts), cross-lesson link, pending suggestion, open flag
tickets.story_text: US-12 / US-19 / US-20 — As a reviewer I need the system to prove, from the stored lesson, that every focus standard is taught *and* checked, that every AI-proposed code waits for a named person, and that a content warning reaches the teacher tip without leaking into student text, so that Approve is refused for the right reasons. This ticket writes the rule bodies; NL-37/38/81 run them, NL-45 serves them.

tickets.title: checks: grounding — quote span, page/chapter range, name scan (`compromise`; blocking in CFU items, advisory elsewhere), `source_ref`, reviewer quote length, `to-clear` rights
tickets.story_text: US-17 / US-18 — As a reviewer I need every quotation, page number and name in a generated lesson to be either from the outline row or flagged, and every excerpt to carry a source and a rights status, so that no invented quote reaches an approved lesson (V-3: 100% sourced or placeholder).

tickets.title: checks: arc continuity advisory rules (R-9)
tickets.story_text: US-12 — As a reviewer I need a quiet hint when a unit's arc drifts (the same opening routine three lessons running, homework that does not match the next lesson, a performance-task skill nobody practises, a vocabulary list over the cap), so that I look at it without it blocking approval. Cuttable (PD-17 #3): if the cut fires this ticket is dropped and the registry keeps its stub.

tickets.title: review: lessons, versions, snapshots, review events, last editor, dependants, approved snapshots
tickets.story_text: US-29 — As anyone who must answer "who changed this lesson, when, and from which version", I need every lesson, every immutable version and every state move stored in one place that can only be appended to. Platform work: Submit (collab), Approve and reopen (web), the board, history and export all read and write through this repository, so it lands before them.

tickets.title: review: safety-flag, alignment-link and suggestion repositories
tickets.story_text: US-19 / US-20 — As a reviewer I clear a safety flag with a note, confirm or remove an AI-proposed standard, and see AI suggestions held outside the lesson; each is a row that names the person and the time. Platform work: the issue list, resolve, assist and coverage tickets read and write these rows.

tickets.title: review: lesson read (derived row or snapshot) and history
tickets.story_text: US-13 / US-14 / US-29 — As a reviewer, author or approver I open a lesson and see everything the workspace and the approval review need in one answer (content, standards with who asserted them, texts, outline row, checklist, dependencies), and I can read its full history: every version, its provenance and every audited action.

tickets.title: review: issue list as of a hash (`pending`), resolutions, safety-flag clear, standard decisions with undo
tickets.story_text: US-16 / US-19 / US-20 / US-21 — As a reviewer I see exactly what is wrong with a lesson and what stops Submit or Approve, I clear a block with a named reason, clear a safety flag with a note, and confirm or remove an AI-proposed standard (with a short undo), so that every approval rests on a person's recorded decision.

tickets.title: review: fill a placeholder or excerpt slot through the collaboration server
tickets.story_text: US-17 / US-18 — As a reviewer I replace a "Reviewer to insert" placeholder or an excerpt slot with a real quote from a source I verified, with its source and rights status, so that the lesson's evidence is real and V-3 (100% of quotes sourced) holds.

tickets.title: review: regenerate as candidate, read, adopt
tickets.story_text: US-22 / US-10 — As a reviewer I can ask for a fresh draft of a lesson without losing the one I have: the new draft arrives beside the current one as a candidate, I read it, and I adopt the whole thing or one section as a recorded edit under my name.

tickets.title: metrics: heartbeats, merged sessions across tabs, frozen first-approval metrics row, board rows (pure + repo + services)
tickets.story_text: US-15 / US-30 — As the person judging whether the tool cut reviewer time, I need review time measured honestly: active minutes only, one person in two tabs counted once, synthetic accounts excluded, and one frozen row per lesson at its first approval, never shown by name. This is the north-star data (M-1) and its guard (M-3, G-2).

tickets.title: evals: evidence repository, eval runner, CLI, suite shells S1–S14, `load/` shells
tickets.story_text: US-36 — As the builder who must show the tool works, I need one runner that executes a named suite, stores one result per case with its source, and writes a report naming the code version, so later tickets only fill suites. Platform work: S1…S14 and the load scripts hang on this.

tickets.title: assist: request and decide an AI rewrite suggestion
tickets.story_text: US-23 — As a reviewer I select a passage, add a note and get a tracked rewrite suggestion held outside the lesson; nothing AI-written enters the lesson until I accept it, and an accepted change is attributed to me and tagged `ai-assist`. Cuttable (PD-17 #8): if the cut fires, the service is dropped and `wiring/assist.ts` stays a stub.

tickets.title: export: idempotent export of approved snapshots (dependants only when their sources are approved)
tickets.story_text: US-35 / US-28 — As an approver I export a unit's approved lessons as a versioned JSON file in the published schema, and exporting twice with no change gives the same file, so Newsela can import what was approved and nothing else. Cuttable (PD-17 #5): if the cut fires the service is dropped and `wiring/exports.ts` stays a stub.

tickets.title: docs: README run and Compose instructions
tickets.story_text: Delivery (no US): the brief requires *Technical Documentation*; a reviewer must be able to run the app from the README alone. NL-139 finalizes it at the release SHA.

tickets.title: review: lesson transitions with every gate re-checked on the server (pin, four-eyes, rating, dependency order, Submit/unfreeze via collab); fills review-area wiring
tickets.story_text: US-24 — As a reviewer I submit a lesson when nothing is blocking, to freeze it, so that the approver reads exactly what I sent. US-25 — As an approver I approve one pinned version on its evidence, so that "approved" means a named person approved exactly that text. US-26/27/28/31 — send back with a reason, approve linked lessons in order, reopen without breaking dependants, rate the draft at Approve.

tickets.title: metrics: unit board and unit metrics from stored rows, aggregate only; fills metrics-area wiring
tickets.story_text: US-11 — As an author or reviewer I need to know which lesson to review next, so that I spend my time where a lesson is furthest from approvable. US-12 — I see that a lesson depends on another. US-30 — I see reviewer time per approved lesson honestly: with its n, the fast-approval guard, "approved k of N" and the caption, never by person.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-2 Units home
tickets.story_text: US-1 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to upload the unit outline as CSV or XLSX and get a numbered version; Units home is where I start that, see each stored version and the latest run (US-6, US-10 entries).

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-3 Upload outline
tickets.story_text: US-1 / US-2 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to upload the unit outline as CSV or XLSX, or paste a public Google Sheet link, and get a fixed, numbered version, so that every later step points at one known input.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-4 Validation report (cell text rendered as text, R-58)
tickets.story_text: US-3 — As an outline author (P-2), I need every row marked OK, warning or error, with the original cell and a proposed fix, so that I fix the outline before any money is spent (with US-4 cell kinds and US-5 ELD re-maps).

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-5 Start run dialog
tickets.story_text: US-6 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to choose which rows to generate, see the prompt version the run will use, and set a spend cap, so that nothing is spent beyond what I chose.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-6 Generation progress (2 s poll, stale banner, run control)
tickets.story_text: US-7 — As an outline author (P-2), I need one tile per lesson that shows where it is and to open finished lessons while others generate; US-8 — failed lessons say why and retry on their own, so I never pay twice.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-7 Unit plan
tickets.story_text: US-9 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to read the one-line plan for every teaching day, what each hands forward, and which lessons link, before reading lessons one by one.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-8 Unit board (sort, filters, north-star tile)
tickets.story_text: US-11 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need to see which lesson to review next, sorted by what blocks, so my time goes where it matters; the same board shows dependency flags (US-12) and the north-star tile (US-30), the reviewer minutes per approved lesson, with its *n* and no baseline claimed.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-9 read view and evidence pane (issue jump-to-span, addresses, asserted-by, R-58)
scope: SCR-9 read view and evidence rail
tickets.story_text: US-13 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need to read the draft in Newsela's own lesson shape, and (US-14) keep the evidence beside the text: issues, standards with their official text, and the confirmed outline row, so I can judge without opening another tab.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-9 live editor (y-prosemirror + provider, presence, stored ack, reconnect, drops refused local edits and tells the typist)
tickets.story_text: US-15 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need to edit the lesson together with colleagues and know my edits are stored, so nothing I type is lost and my time is counted fairly; when the lesson freezes under me, the editor must say plainly which of my edits were not kept (SP-2).

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-9 workspace actions (standard confirm/remove + 6 s undo, start review, submit with reasons, withdraw, regenerate entry, heartbeat sender)
tickets.story_text: US-16/US-18/US-20 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need to confirm or remove a tool-chosen standard (with an undo), start and submit review, withdraw, and ask for a regenerated candidate, with every disabled button saying why; my active time is recorded by heartbeat and shown only as unit totals (US-14 disclosure).

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-10 Insert quote or excerpt
tickets.story_text: US-17/US-18 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need to fill a quote placeholder or an excerpt slot with real text, its source and its rights status, so every quote in an approved lesson is a person's sourced choice.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-11 Resolve or clear
tickets.story_text: US-20/US-21 — As a reviewer (P-1), or an approver clearing a safety flag, I need to record a named resolution for a blocking issue fixed outside the tool, or clear a safety flag with a note, so the record says plainly what a person decided.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-12 Candidate compare
tickets.story_text: US-22 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need a regenerated candidate shown beside the current lesson, section by section, so I can adopt the whole candidate, one section, or leave it, without losing the current lesson.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-14 Approval review (checklist, pin, rating, stale 409)
tickets.story_text: US-25/US-27/US-31 — As an approver (P-3) I need to read one submitted lesson exactly as frozen, check each checklist item against its evidence, rate the draft, and approve that pinned version, one lesson at a time.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-15 Send back or reopen
tickets.story_text: US-26/US-28 — As an approver (P-3) I need to send a submitted lesson back with a reason tag and a note, or reopen an approved lesson with a reason, so the author knows what to fix and the record shows who decided.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-16 History and provenance
tickets.story_text: US-29 — As an approver (P-3) I need every version of a lesson with its hash and provenance, and the audit log, so the lesson can be defended to a state reviewer.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-17 Run summary
tickets.story_text: US-32 — As an approver (P-3) I need one summary per run (what the batch cost and how clean it was), and (US-36) the numbers behind the page-speed and generation-time claims, each with its n, so the unit's cost and quality can be stated honestly.

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-13 AI assist panel
tickets.story_text: US-23 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need to rewrite a selected passage from my note as a suggestion I accept or reject, so AI help is visible, optional and never silent (cut #8: the whole panel can be dropped).

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-18 Coverage matrix
tickets.story_text: US-33 — As an approver (P-3) I need a read-only standard × lesson grid showing where each standard is introduced, practised or assessed and who confirmed it, so gaps in a unit are visible before export (cut #4).

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-19 Unit quality
tickets.story_text: US-34/US-36 — As an approver (P-3) I need the unit's draft-quality, health and seeded-error numbers, each with its n and an honest label, so I can judge whether the generated lessons can be trusted (cut #6).

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-20 Export
tickets.story_text: US-35 — As an approver (P-3) I need to write a versioned export of the approved snapshots and see which lessons are held back because a lesson they link to is not approved (US-28), so nothing half-ready leaves the tool (cut #5).

tickets.title: web-ui: SCR-21 Prompt guidance
tickets.story_text: US-10 — As an outline author (P-2) I need to edit the guidance layer of the prompt as numbered versions with a reason, and try it on one lesson, so I can tweak the output without touching the locked rules (cut #7).

tickets.title: intake: validation report read and intake choices (`default` vs confirmed by name)
anchor: FE-4 counts on the issued sheet
tickets.story_text: US-3 — As an author I need to see every problem in the outline before any money is spent, with Generate kept off until every error is confirmed, so that a bad code never reaches 47 paid model calls. US-4 and US-5 — I confirm what each cell really is and keep or re-map an ELD label, so that the lesson cites the state's standard.

tickets.title: runs: progress, unit plan, control, summary; fills runs wiring
tickets.story_text: US-7 — As an author I watch the lessons being written (one tile per lesson with running cost) so I can see the run is healthy. US-8 — I recover from failures without paying twice (cancel, retry failed, resume). US-9 — I read the unit plan first. US-32 — I read the run summary (cost, retries, failures, calls lost, brakes fired).

tickets.title: generation: worker wiring — real queue, adapters, recorder, spend, store; capture through the real claim loop on the stub
scope: stub-provider capture through the real claim loop
tickets.story_text: US-7 — As an author (P-2) I need to watch lessons being written and open the finished ones; US-8 — I need a killed or failed run to carry on without paying twice. This ticket is the join that makes both true: it wires every generation piece built so far into one running worker and proves, on the stub provider, that a queued run really becomes stored lessons.

tickets.title: collab: Hocuspocus server — socket auth from the app session, per-update write guard with `refused`/`refused_from`, debounced persistence, `stored`/`mode` acks; fills collab server wiring
tickets.story_text: US-15 — As a reviewer I edit together with a colleague and know my time is counted fairly, so that two of us can finish a lesson together without losing each other's work. Platform: this is the only process that writes lesson content (R-26), and the one that refuses typing after Submit.

tickets.title: checks: check job runner in its own worker lane (issues, alignment links, dependants re-queued); fills checks wiring
tickets.story_text: US-16/US-17/US-20 (with US-14, US-18, US-24, US-25) — As a reviewer I see a new blocking issue within seconds of an edit, so that what blocks Submit and Approve is always current. Platform: after every durable store, the deterministic suite runs in its own worker lane so checks never wait behind generation.

tickets.title: ops: seed CDE standards, prompt v1, one demo account per role
tickets.story_text: US-37 — As a staff member I sign in and see only what my role can do, so that only an author starts a run and only an approver approves. Platform: the demo needs the official standards tables, the first prompt version and one account per role to exist on a fresh database (R-4, R-54).

tickets.title: ops: health routes on web/worker/collab, process start events, backup script, sample-builder event
tickets.story_text: Platform ticket (no user story): the deploy and the recording need liveness probes, an auditable start of every process, a verified database backup after the full run (PD-30) and a logged sample build. It serves US-36 (trust the build's numbers) indirectly: the backup is what protects the full-run evidence.

tickets.title: evals: S1 intake golden and S7 safety-note cases
tickets.story_text: US-3 — As an author I see every problem in the outline before any money is spent. US-36 — As the builder I trust the numbers before the demo: the intake and safety golden suites run in the merge gate and prove the deterministic layer is right before any model is paid.

tickets.title: evals: S2 check golden and S4 grounding plants
tickets.story_text: US-36 — As the builder I trust the numbers before the demo: every blocking rule has a failing fixture that proves it fires, and the invention scans catch the planted quotes, pages and names, with few false flags on clean lessons.

tickets.title: evals: full-run driver over the OpenAPI (Prism-tested) and S9/S13 report builder from stored rows
tickets.story_text: US-36 — As the builder I trust the build's numbers before the demo: a full 47-day run of the issued unit, driven through the product's own HTTP API, with a report whose every number is read from stored rows (R-51), so the video never states a number the database cannot back.

tickets.title: evals: spike report importer (SP-1…SP-3)
tickets.story_text: Platform ticket (no user story): the three spikes (SP-1 one-call draft, SP-2 freeze at Submit, SP-3 invention scans) ran before the database existed. Their results must land in `experiment_run` and `model_call` once it does, so build spend (M-29) and the spike evidence are queryable like any other record (R-48).

tickets.title: prompts: save a guidance version and try it on one lesson
tickets.story_text: US-10 — As an author I change the guidance part of the prompt and try it on one lesson first, while the locked rules stay out of reach, so that I can improve drafts without breaking the rules that keep them safe. (Cut #7: if cut, the list and the locked layer remain, NL-34.)

tickets.title: judge: OpenRouter adapter, judge job, verdict repository
tickets.story_text: Platform ticket (cut #2, no user story of its own): a binary, advisory, provisional judge on a second provider (PD-12) reads one activity and one official standard and answers "does it teach this?". It adds a second provider key and sends lesson text off-box, so it is security work.

tickets.title: integration: CON-1 sign-in end to end (SCR-1 on the real backend)
scope: SCR-1 against the real session routes
real-stack e2e harness for every later integration ticket
tickets.story_text: US-37 — As staff I sign in and see only what my role can do.
